sentence: AI-made images are illustration only.
same: An AI-made image may serve only as an illustration.
flip: An AI-made image may serve as a screenshot or as proof.

sentence: Every reply is written once, for one conversation.
same: Write each reply a single time, for a single conversation.
flip: Write each reply once and reuse it across several conversations.

sentence: Give the point a reply should make, never paste-ready text.
same: Supply the point a reply should make, and not text ready to paste.
flip: Supply the point a reply should make, always as text ready to paste.

sentence: An occasional connect post is allowed in the `other` lane, at most 1 in 15 originals
same: A connect post may go in the other lane, no more than 1 in every 15 originals.
flip: A connect post may go in the other lane, at least 1 in every 15 originals.

sentence: Never tag a person, and never a premium vendor.
same: Do not tag a person, and do not tag a premium vendor.
flip: Always tag the person, and always tag a premium vendor.

sentence: A shout-out is a reply, so the Replies no-repeat rule covers it: never one line under several makers' posts
same: A shout-out counts as a reply, so the no-repeat rule applies: the same line is not posted under several makers' posts.
flip: A shout-out counts as a reply, so the no-repeat rule applies: post the same line under several makers' posts.

sentence: Repost only a maker's release post, never your own post and never someone's mega-list of alternatives.
same: Repost a maker's release post and nothing else, not your own post and not someone's mega-list of alternatives.
flip: Repost a maker's release post, your own post and someone's mega-list of alternatives.

sentence: Quote only a maker's news.
same: A quote should be of a maker's news and nothing else.
flip: Quote any post you like, not only a maker's news.

sentence: Concrete numbers only if the draft's verify run sourced them
same: Use a concrete number only when the draft's verify run has sourced it.
flip: Use a concrete number even when the draft's verify run has not sourced it.

sentence: The root post stands alone: a stranger who sees only the root gets the whole payoff.
same: The root has to work by itself: someone who sees only the root receives the entire payoff.
flip: The root depends on the replies: someone who sees only the root does not receive the payoff.

sentence: Under 280 characters when possible, never over 600.
same: Aim for under 280 characters, and stay at or below 600.
flip: Aim for under 280 characters, and go over 600 when it helps.

sentence: One difference per post.
same: Each post carries a single difference.
flip: Each post carries several differences.

sentence: no two shout-outs share wording
same: Each shout-out is worded differently from every other.
flip: Shout-outs reuse the same wording.

sentence: Offer it once per draft, never as a condition.
same: A test should be offered a single time per draft, and never made a condition.
flip: A test should be offered repeatedly per draft, and made a condition.

sentence: Name the job the free tool does, never "replaces" or a promised 1:1 swap.
same: Describe the job the free tool does, without saying it replaces the paid one or promising a 1:1 swap.
flip: Say the free tool replaces the paid one, and promise a 1:1 swap.

sentence: Say "open source" only when `CLAIMS.md` shows it.
same: Call a tool open source only when the CLAIMS.md rows show it.
flip: Call a tool open source whether or not the CLAIMS.md rows show it.

sentence: one PAID → FREE parent every other day
same: A PAID → FREE post goes up on alternate days.
flip: A PAID → FREE post goes up every day.

sentence: this run left `APPROVED` untouched.
same: The run did not touch the APPROVED file.
flip: The run created the APPROVED file.

sentence: The operator does every paste and post; this skill has no X write access.
same: Every paste and post is done by the operator, and this skill cannot write to X.
flip: The skill pastes and posts to X for the operator.

sentence: The lesson must be `adopted` with rule `none`.
same: A lesson qualifies only when it is adopted and its rule state is none.
flip: A lesson qualifies only when it is adopted and its rule state is already applied.
